children: U.S. STOCK INDEXES SWING LOWER AS OIL, YIELDS JUMP
Wall Street's three main indexes turned lower on Tuesday, with the Dow Industrials
leading losses amid broad pressure from a rally in oil prices and climbing Treasury yields.
The Dow's biggest loser is Johnson & Johnson
after news late on Monday that an experimental depression drug it developed with Contineum Therapeutics
failed to meet the main goal of a mid-stage study. Contineum shares tumbled more than 11% as a result.

Meanwhile, U.S. 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest levels since 2007 as investors bet that the Federal Reserve will kick off a series of rate increases next week as it battles stubborn inflation.

Oil prices are higher after attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure left the kingdom's East-West Pipeline offline, raising fears that damage to energy infrastructure and transport routes could take longer to repair.
is the sole gainer among the S&P 500's
11 major industry sectors, adding more than 1%. Consumer Discretionary
is the biggest laggard, off more than 1.2%.
Here is your morning snapshot from 10:15 a.m. ET (1415 GMT):
Main US equity indexes red; Dow leads losses down ~1%
Consumer Discretionary is weakest S&P 500 sector; energy sole gainer
Dollar gains slightly; US crude up >2%; gold slips; bitcoin falls >3%
US 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.041%, highest since 2007, now ~5.01%
